verses.pali: “Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇe āpanno ca bhikkhu codako ca bhikkhu na sādhukaṁ attanāva attānaṁ paccavekkhati tasmetaṁ, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇe pāṭikaṅkhaṁ:
verses.english: “Mendicants, in a disciplinary issue, if neither the offending mendicant nor the accusing mendicant carefully checks themselves, you can expect that issue

verses.pali: ‘dīghattāya kharattāya vāḷattāya saṁvattissati, bhikkhū ca na phāsuṁ viharissantī’ti.
verses.english: will lead to lasting acrimony and enmity, and the mendicants won’t live comfortably.

verses.pali: Yasmiñca kho, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇe āpanno ca bhikkhu codako ca bhikkhu sādhukaṁ attanāva attānaṁ paccavekkhati tasmetaṁ, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇe pāṭikaṅkhaṁ:
verses.english: But in a disciplinary issue, if both the offending mendicant and the accusing mendicant carefully check themselves, you can expect that issue

verses.pali: ‘na dīghattāya kharattāya vāḷattāya saṁvattissati, bhikkhū ca phāsuṁ viharissantī’ti.
verses.english: won’t lead to lasting acrimony and enmity, and the mendicants will live comfortably.

verses.pali: Kathañca, bhikkhave, āpanno bhikkhu sādhukaṁ attanāva attānaṁ paccavekkhati?
verses.english: And how, mendicants, does an offending mendicant carefully check themselves?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, āpanno bhikkhu iti paṭisañcikkhati:
verses.english: An offending mendicant reflects:

verses.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho akusalaṁ āpanno kañcideva desaṁ kāyena.
verses.english: ‘I have committed a certain unskillful offense with the body.

verses.pali: Maṁ so bhikkhu addasa akusalaṁ āpajjamānaṁ kañcideva desaṁ kāyena.
verses.english: That mendicant saw me do this.

verses.pali: No ce ahaṁ akusalaṁ āpajjeyyaṁ kañcideva desaṁ kāyena, na maṁ so bhikkhu passeyya akusalaṁ āpajjamānaṁ kañcideva desaṁ kāyena.
verses.english: If I hadn’t committed that offense, they wouldn’t have seen me.

verses.pali: Yasmā ca kho, ahaṁ akusalaṁ āpanno kañcideva desaṁ kāyena, tasmā maṁ so bhikkhu addasa akusalaṁ āpajjamānaṁ kañcideva desaṁ kāyena.
verses.english: But since I did commit that offense, they did see me.

verses.pali: Disvā ca pana maṁ so bhikkhu akusalaṁ āpajjamānaṁ kañcideva desaṁ kāyena anattamano ahosi.
verses.english: When they saw me, they were upset,

verses.pali: Anattamano samāno anattamanavacanaṁ maṁ so bhikkhu avaca.
verses.english: and they voiced their unhappiness to me.

verses.pali: Anattamanavacanāhaṁ tena bhikkhunā vutto samāno anattamano ahosiṁ.
verses.english: Then I also got upset,

verses.pali: Anattamano samāno paresaṁ ārocesiṁ.
verses.english: so I told others.

verses.pali: Iti mameva tattha accayo accagamā suṅkadāyakaṁva bhaṇḍasmin’ti.
verses.english: So the mistake is mine alone, like someone who owes customs duty on their goods.’

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, āpanno bhikkhu sādhukaṁ attanāva attānaṁ paccavekkhati.
verses.english: That’s how, mendicants, an offending mendicant carefully checks themselves.

verses.pali: Kathañca, bhikkhave, codako bhikkhu sādhukaṁ attanāva attānaṁ paccavekkhati?
verses.english: And how, mendicants, does an accusing mendicant carefully check themselves?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, codako bhikkhu iti paṭisañcikkhati:
verses.english: An accusing mendicant reflects:

verses.pali: ‘ayaṁ kho bhikkhu akusalaṁ āpanno kañcideva desaṁ kāyena.
verses.english: ‘This mendicant has committed a certain unskillful offense with the body.

verses.pali: Ahaṁ imaṁ bhikkhuṁ addasaṁ akusalaṁ āpajjamānaṁ kañcideva desaṁ kāyena.
verses.english: I saw them do that.

verses.pali: No ce ayaṁ bhikkhu akusalaṁ āpajjeyya kañcideva desaṁ kāyena, nāhaṁ imaṁ bhikkhuṁ passeyyaṁ akusalaṁ āpajjamānaṁ kañcideva desaṁ kāyena.
verses.english: If they hadn’t committed that offense, I wouldn’t have seen them.

verses.pali: Yasmā ca kho, ayaṁ bhikkhu akusalaṁ āpanno kañcideva desaṁ kāyena, tasmā ahaṁ imaṁ bhikkhuṁ addasaṁ akusalaṁ āpajjamānaṁ kañcideva desaṁ kāyena.
verses.english: But since they did commit that offense, I did see them.

verses.pali: Disvā ca panāhaṁ imaṁ bhikkhuṁ akusalaṁ āpajjamānaṁ kañcideva desaṁ kāyena anattamano ahosiṁ.
verses.english: When I saw them, I was upset,

verses.pali: Anattamano samāno anattamanavacanāhaṁ imaṁ bhikkhuṁ avacaṁ.
verses.english: and I voiced my unhappiness to them.

verses.pali: Anattamanavacanāyaṁ bhikkhu mayā vutto samāno anattamano ahosi.
verses.english: Then they also got upset,

verses.pali: Anattamano samāno paresaṁ ārocesi.
verses.english: so they told others.

verses.pali: Iti mameva tattha accayo accagamā suṅkadāyakaṁva bhaṇḍasmin’ti.
verses.english: So the mistake is mine alone, like someone who owes customs duty on their goods.’

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, codako bhikkhu sādhukaṁ attanāva attānaṁ paccavekkhati.
verses.english: That’s how, mendicants, an accusing mendicant carefully checks themselves.

verses.pali: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇe āpanno ca bhikkhu codako ca bhikkhu na sādhukaṁ attanāva attānaṁ paccavekkhati tasmetaṁ, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇe pāṭikaṅkhaṁ dīghattāya kharattāya vāḷattāya saṁvattissati, bhikkhū ca na phāsuṁ viharissantīti.
verses.english: In a disciplinary issue, if neither the offending mendicant nor the accusing mendicant carefully checks themselves, you can expect that issue will lead to lasting acrimony and enmity, and the mendicants won’t live comfortably.

verses.pali: Yasmiñca kho, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇe āpanno ca bhikkhu codako ca bhikkhu sādhukaṁ attanāva attānaṁ paccavekkhati tasmetaṁ, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇe pāṭikaṅkhaṁ na dīghattāya kharattāya vāḷattāya saṁvattissati, bhikkhū ca phāsuṁ viharissantī”ti.
verses.english: But in a disciplinary issue, if both the offending mendicant and the accusing mendicant carefully checks themselves, you can expect that issue won’t lead to lasting acrimony and enmity, and the mendicants will live comfortably.”
